reasons: The table is hand-written and covers only listed countries.
No tests are visible in this packet.
Some placements are not explained in the code.

terms.meaning: A list where a value is found by its key, here a country name.
A standard short code for a country, such as US or GB.
Making letters small and removing spaces at the edges, so that matches are exact.
A fixed set of colours chosen for a design.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and design rules
sections.what: A comment at the top explains that region is computed from the country, never stored, and that unknown countries get a neutral Unknown label.
sections.why: The rule is stated in the comment: never guess a region that cannot be mapped.

sections.name: RegionName
sections.title: Region names and their colours
sections.what: Defines the seven region names used by this file and passes the shared palette through as the colour for each region.
sections.why: Gives the rest of the chart one consistent set of region names and colours.
sections.watch_out: The palette keys must match these region names, which cannot be checked from this file alone.

sections.name: REGION_ORDER
sections.title: Order of regions in the legend
sections.what: Lists the regions in the canonical legend order, with Unknown last.
sections.why: Gives the legend a predictable order.
sections.watch_out: The house order in bubbleDimensions.ts is a different list, so the two orders can disagree.

sections.name: COUNTRY_REGION (part 1)
sections.title: Countries in the Americas and Europe
sections.what: Maps country names and two-letter codes for North America, Latin America and Europe to their region.
sections.why: Covers the common spellings and codes found in the data.
sections.watch_out: Keys must be in lower case and without edge spaces, or they will never match.

sections.name: COUNTRY_REGION (part 2)
sections.title: Countries in Europe and Asia
sections.what: Continues the table with the rest of Europe, then Asia, including China, India, Japan, Korea, Pakistan, South East Asia and Kazakhstan.
sections.why: Gives the chart a region for the main Asian and European countries in the data.
sections.watch_out: Some placements are judgement calls, such as Kazakhstan under Asia, and the code gives no reason for them.

sections.name: COUNTRY_REGION (part 3)
sections.title: Middle East, Africa and Oceania
sections.what: Continues the table with Middle East and Africa countries, such as Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey, Iran and Nigeria, and the two Oceania countries listed, Australia and New Zealand.
sections.why: Covers the region the house deck later splits into Middle East and Africa.
sections.watch_out: Most other Oceania and Pacific countries are missing, so they become Unknown.

sections.name: regionForCountry
sections.title: Looking up a country's region
sections.what: Takes a country name, cleans it up, looks it up, and returns its region. Empty or unlisted countries return Unknown.
sections.why: Gives every project a region, while being honest when one cannot be found.
sections.watch_out: Unknown here becomes Other in bubbleDimensions.ts, so the two labels do not match up.

summary: Works out a region name for a project from its country, using a fixed, hand-written lookup table.
purpose: Lets the bubble chart group projects by region, even though the data does not store a region.
why: The header comment says region is never stored on the project, so it is worked out from the country each time, and an unmapped country is shown as Unknown rather than guessed.
how: 1. Removes spaces at the edges and lowercases the country name. 2. Looks it up in the table of country names and two-letter codes. 3. Returns the region found, or Unknown if there is no match. The table is split into three parts for reading.
inputs: A country name or code as text, or nothing.
outputs: One of the seven region names, including Unknown.
risks: The table only covers the listed countries, so many others, including most Pacific islands, become Unknown. Some placements are judgement calls the code does not explain, such as Kazakhstan under Asia and Russia under Europe. Short codes such as no and in are ordinary words and could match unintended text.
debug: If a project lands in Unknown, check its country spelling against the table, then add the lowercase name or code if it is missing. If a country is in the wrong region, check its entry.
